items.title: The degree-n part of a finitely generated graded module is a finite module over the degree-zero ring
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.source_version: Stacks Project git a04446e57ec1 (2026-07-28); file algebra.tex; corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: If M is a finitely generated graded module over a graded ring S which is finitely generated over S_0, the lemma states that each graded piece M_n is a finite S_0-module (statement lines 14089-14094). The proof does not use Hilbert functions or a Noetherian hypothesis: it replaces the generators by their homogeneous components, arranges the algebra generators in positive degrees, and then exhibits each M_n as generated over S_0 by the finitely many monomials of degree n in the algebra generators times the module generators (proof lines 14096-14104). The reduction to homogeneous generators is what makes the graded bookkeeping possible, and the author writes it out. H2.
